topStories.headline: Hayes Valley Launches Official Entertainment Zone, Bringing To-Go Drinks to the Promenade Every Weekend
topStories.dek: The neighborhood's new Entertainment Zone designation lets 21+ visitors sip cocktails, beer, and wine outdoors on the Hayes Promenade every Friday and Saturday.
topStories.body:
Hayes Valley has officially become one of San Francisco's designated Entertainment Zones, allowing visitors 21 and older to purchase to-go alcoholic beverages from participating bars and restaurants and enjoy them outdoors along the Hayes Promenade. The zone, announced by Supervisor Bilal Mahmood and organized by the Hayes Valley Merchants Council in cooperation with the Hayes Valley Neighborhood Association and the Hayes Promenade, soft-launched on the same day as the annual Hayes Valley Carnival in July and held its official kickoff with live music on July 24–25.

Under the new rules, the EZ is active every Friday from 4 p.m. to 10 p.m. and every Saturday from noon to 10 p.m. Eleven bars and restaurants are currently participating. Visitors must be 21 or older, show ID, and wear a wristband obtained from participating businesses. Drinks must remain within the EZ boundaries.

The launch comes amid a citywide expansion of Entertainment Zones. According to SFist, San Francisco now has 30 such zones, and businesses within them have reported major boosts in sales. The mayor's office previously noted that participating businesses saw sales increases of at least 700 percent during EZ events.

Not everyone is enthusiastic. A commentary on hvsafe.com argues that the EZ model favors consolidated commercial interests and could undermine Hayes Valley's long-standing formula retail ban, which was established in 2004 to protect independent businesses. Community members who share those concerns are encouraged to engage with the Hayes Valley Neighborhood Association.

topStories.headline: Two-Alarm Fire Displaces Residents at Tenderloin Apartment Building on Jones Street
topStories.dek: A July 19 blaze at 424 Jones Street spread through the light shaft of the six-story building, leaving an unknown number of residents displaced and three treated for smoke inhalation.
topStories.body:
A two-alarm fire broke out on the morning of Sunday, July 19, at a six-story residential apartment building at 424 Jones Street in the Tenderloin, according to the San Francisco Fire Department. The blaze began around 11:39 a.m. on the building's first floor and spread to multiple floors via the building's light shaft, which channels light into interior kitchens and bathrooms.

Residents were evacuated and three people were evaluated for smoke inhalation; one was transported to a hospital. San Francisco firefighters declared the fire extinguished as of 1:54 p.m. The San Francisco Department of Emergency Management issued an alert asking the public to avoid the Jones and Ellis area while crews worked the scene.

The Red Cross was called to the scene to assist displaced residents. The exact number of households displaced was not immediately known, and the cause of the fire remained under investigation as of the time of reporting, according to SFFD spokesperson Lt. Mariano Elias.

The fire comes as the Tenderloin continues to grapple with housing vulnerability. City officials and community organizations including the Tenderloin Community Benefit District have been working on broader neighborhood stabilization efforts, including a storefront grant program designed to fill vacant ground-floor commercial spaces and support new small businesses on key corridors including Larkin Street.

topStories.headline: Mid-Market and Tenderloin See New Storefronts as $60M Downtown Fund Takes Shape
topStories.dek: A wave of small businesses is opening in the Tenderloin under a city grant program, while Mayor Lurie's San Francisco Downtown Development Corporation targets Mid-Market as part of a $60 million private recovery fund.
topStories.body:
Vacant storefronts in the Tenderloin are finding new life through the Tenderloin Storefront Opportunity Grant Program, overseen by the Office of Economic and Workforce Development. The program offers eligible businesses up to $50,000 for first-time storefronts and up to $75,000 for businesses expanding from elsewhere in the city, funds that can be applied to equipment, tenant improvements, and operating expenses.

Among recent recipients highlighted by Mission Local in June 2026: Tender Hearts Thrift, a secondhand shop opening at 683 O'Farrell St.; Ruru Kitchen, a cafe from Ecuadorian industrial designer Francisco Bastidas backed by a $75,000 grant; and Tender Noodle, a new noodle restaurant coming to 721 Larkin St. A total of 39 businesses citywide received more than $3 million in this round of OEWD funding, with four of those new shops located in the Tenderloin. According to OEWD data cited by the SF Examiner, the storefront vacancy rate on Larkin Street sits at approximately 25 percent.

At the same time, the broader Mid-Market corridor is drawing attention from the San Francisco Downtown Development Corporation (DDC), a nonprofit public benefit corporation formed in 2025. The DDC announced over $60 million in contributions and commitments from philanthropic, corporate, and individual partners — including Google, Amazon, OpenAI, and Ripple — in December 2025. The DDC's work covers Mid-Market, parts of SoMa, Civic Center, the Financial District, and the Embarcadero. Its current initiatives include expanded clean-and-safe services, a Downtown Business Fund to reduce storefront vacancies, and support for the Downtown First Thursdays event series, which drew over 300,000 visitors in 2025.

Analysts and neighborhood advocates note that sustained progress will also depend on addressing persistent open-air drug activity, particularly after dark, which has deterred foot traffic and business investment in Mid-Market for years.

moreNews.headline: Tenderloin Museum Moving Ahead with Landmark Expansion — 'Boxing in the Bay' Opens This Summer
moreNews.body: The Tenderloin Museum is in the midst of its most ambitious expansion to date: a $3.7 million capital campaign to open a new 6,850-square-foot space adjacent to its current Eddy Street location, tripling the museum's footprint. The new space — a historic former boxing gym that once hosted Muhammad Ali, Jack Dempsey, and George Foreman between 1924 and 1992 — is slated to eventually house a neon sign gallery, an expanded permanent collection, and a dedicated arts gallery. This summer, the museum is opening a pop-up exhibition titled 'Boxing in the Bay,' drawing on rare photographs, ephemera, and oral histories from the Newman's Gym era to bring San Francisco's boxing legacy to life. The museum is located at 398 Eddy St. in the Tenderloin.

moreNews.headline: SF Symphony Summer Season Brings Andrew Bird, A.R. Rahman, and Film Concerts to Davies Hall
moreNews.body: The San Francisco Symphony's 2026 summer season at Davies Symphony Hall, 201 Van Ness Ave., features an eclectic lineup running through August and into the fall. Highlights include a live orchestral performance accompanying Andrew Bird on August 1, and a film-in-concert series that includes Matilda (July 25–26, hosted by Danny DeVito), West Side Story, and James Bond Forever. Classical programs are led by conductors Nicolas Ellis and Chloé Van Soeterstède, with solo performances by violinists Paul Huang and Geneva Lewis. The new 2026–27 season, titled 'Forward Motion,' launches in September under Executive Artistic Director Terence Blanchard with over 300 shows planned across nine months.

moreNews.headline: SFJAZZ Center Announces 2026–27 Season 'Forward Motion' with Terence Blanchard at the Helm
moreNews.body: SFJAZZ has announced its 2026–27 season, 'Forward Motion,' led by new Executive Artistic Director Terence Blanchard and CEO Gabrielle Armand. The season spans nine months and over 300 shows at the center's home at 201 Franklin St. in Hayes Valley, celebrating centennials of Miles Davis, John Coltrane, Antonio Carlos Jobim, and Ray Brown, along with performances by icons including Ron Carter, Dianne Reeves, and Branford Marsalis. The summer Summerfest series, a six-week celebration of musical traditions across the Americas running July through August, is currently underway. Upcoming on the published calendar: Brad Mehldau's 'Ride Into the Sun' at Oakland's Paramount Theatre on August 29, and Christian McBride at the Miner Auditorium on September 10–11.

moreNews.headline: Asian Art Museum's 'FX Harsono: Writing in the Rain' Continues Through September 7
moreNews.body: The Asian Art Museum, 200 Larkin St. in Civic Center, is currently showing 'FX Harsono: Writing in the Rain,' a poetic video installation on view through September 7, 2026. In the work, the Indonesian artist's act of writing his own name becomes a reclamation of erased identity. The museum is also showing 'Al-An deSouza: Table Settings' through November 2 and its new exhibition 'One Hundred Plays of the Noh Theater by Tsukioka Kogyo,' which opened July 16 and runs through February 21, 2027. General admission is free on the first Sunday of each month.
